market_regime: RISK-OFF: day 2 of a broad AI-infrastructure unwind on buildout-cost and credit fears (record CDS at ORCL/CRWV/GOOGL/SpaceX, HPE component-shortage and neocloud-financing comments). All 14 qualifying gappers were gap-DOWNS; zero gap-ups in the watchlist.

gappers.catalyst: Second day of a credit-driven unwind: 5y CDS at a record ~1,314bp and 2031 bonds yielding near 18%, plus HPE's CEO saying its financing arm deliberately avoids lending to neocloud operators.
gappers.catalyst_detail: CRWV fell 11.8% on 11/24 and gapped down again pre-market 11/25, giving back all of Monday's +22.3% squeeze. There was no earnings release or 8-K; the driver is credit. CoreWeave's five-year CDS spread blew out to a record ~1,314bp and its 2031 bonds fell more than 1.6c on the dollar to yield nearly 18%. HPE CEO Antonio Neri's comment that HPE's financing arm deliberately will not lend to neoclouds hardened the funding narrative. Total debt including leases was $66.2B at end-Sept 2026.
gappers.why: Mechanism is cost-of-capital, not demand. A leveraged neocloud whose model depends on continuous debt issuance reprices violently when its own credit spreads blow out; equity is the residual claim, so an 18% bond yield mechanically compresses equity value and forces levered/momentum holders out.
gappers.impact: Looks sustainable as a trend, not a one-day spike. 61.6M shares on the prior session is well above normal and this is day 2 of the unwind, with sector read-through confirmed across NBIS, IREN, ORCL and record CDS at Oracle/Alphabet/SpaceX. Monday's +22% rally failing completely in one session is distribution, not accumulation.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing - the account is 100% cash with 0 open positions, so all 3 weekly trade slots are free. But it cannot clear the Entry Checklist: no bullish catalyst (the catalyst is bearish), sector momentum is down, and price < 200-SMA kills the confluence requirement. A long here would need a stop below an undefined low while credit spreads are still widening, so a sane 7-10% stop cannot produce 2:1 R:R against no identifiable target. Pass; it is only a short/avoid name, and the strategy is long-only.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: SHORT_TERM: this is a falling-knife downtrend, not a long setup. Price is far below the 200-SMA, so the long-bias filter in TRADING-STRATEGY.md blocks it outright; any bounce is a headline-driven fade.

gappers.catalyst: AI-neocloud funding fears: -11.5% on 11/24 after HPE's margin/supply warning, extending the unwind from the 11/12 Q3 guidance cut to the low end on data-center capacity slipping into 1H27.
gappers.catalyst_detail: Nebius guided 2026 revenue to the low end of its range on the 11/12 Q3 report, blaming third-party data-center capacity slipping into 1H27, while raising 2026 capex toward ~$27B. At least seven brokers have cut targets since. It then fell ~16% on one session, bounced ~22% on 11/23 on the Jensen Huang reinstatement headline, and gave it all back (-11.5%) on 11/24 as HPE's lower margin outlook cooled the AI complex. 2027 plans reportedly call for $40-45B of capex against $12-13B of revenue, funded largely by customer prepayments and asset-backed loans.
gappers.why: A capex-to-revenue gap of roughly 3.5x funded by prepayments and asset-backed debt is only viable while credit is cheap and available. The same credit repricing hitting CRWV re-rates NBIS on identical logic, and the guidance cut removed the growth story that justified the multiple.
gappers.impact: Sustainable downtrend. 28.7M shares is heavy, and the fact that a +22% one-day rally was fully reversed within a session says sellers are using strength for exits. Read-through is sector-wide and symmetric with CRWV/IREN - these names are now trading as one credit basket, which is also a correlation-gate problem.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (0 positions, 3 trade slots open). Within today's own list it is the second-best-ranked gapper, but every top-5 name is a gap-DOWN in the same AI-infra/credit theme, so taking any two of them would also trip the >0.75 correlation gate. R:R fails: no defined support, 2:1 would require a target that implies calling the exact bottom of an active credit unwind. Research only - no entry.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: SHORT_TERM: headline/credit driven with no durable long thesis; the structural news (guidance cut, capex blowout) is negative, so there is nothing to carry past the session.

gappers.catalyst: No fresh company news found; continuation of the post-Q3 derating (slumped ~10% postmarket on 11/10 on a disappointing bottom line) now compounded by the broad high-beta risk-off.
gappers.catalyst_detail: Amprius posted record Q3 revenue on 11/10 but missed on the bottom line and sold off ~10% after hours. Four brokers cut targets (Roth to $19 from $22, B. Riley to $16 from $22, Clear Street to $26 from $30, Craig-Hallum trimmed) while keeping Buy ratings. The company's 2026 target is ~$140-145M revenue with >=28% gross margin. Older overhangs remain: a short-seller report alleging misconduct and a Block & Leviton securities-fraud investigation announced in May. No dated 11/24-11/25 catalyst surfaced; at $5.31 it is near the bottom of its 52-week range and below the 200-SMA.
gappers.why: Mechanism is beta plus a broken story. A pre-profit battery name with a legal overhang and a recent earnings miss has no bid when high-beta AI/defense-adjacent growth is being sold; the late-Sept $75M DoW grant pop has fully round-tripped.
gappers.impact: Reads as part of the broad spike rather than stock-specific, and 5.4M shares is modest in absolute terms - this is the thinnest-liquidity name in the top 5. Lower-quality tape means wider slippage and a higher chance of a sharp mean-reverting bounce, but with no catalyst to drive it. Sector read-through is to the small-cap battery/defense complex generally, not a specific peer.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Free slot-wise (0 open positions), but it is the weakest candidate on today's list and would displace capacity better spent on a real setup. Its 20% cap would be ~$20k of equity in a $5 stock with an unresolved fraud investigation. 2:1 R:R is theoretically reachable off the 52-week low with analyst targets at $16-19, but that requires the legal overhang to clear and the tape to turn - not a 7-10% stop trade today. Pass.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: SHORT_TERM: no structural catalyst at all - just beta drift and a post-earnings derating, so there is nothing to hold for.

gappers.catalyst: WSJ reported 11/24 the Pentagon is in talks with General Motors to ramp drone production, read as competitive threat to drone-component suppliers; UMAC slid ~7% on the day.
gappers.catalyst_detail: UMAC is down ~47% in a month. The 11/24 trigger was a WSJ report that the Pentagon is in talks with GM (and reportedly Ford) to scale drone manufacturing - directly threatening to UMAC, which sells motors and components that automakers could in-source. This lands on top of a Q3 report (11/5) where revenue rose 551% y/y to $13.9M and beat, but management WITHDREW full-year revenue guidance citing slower defense contract awards and the Gauntlet II evaluation outcome, and gross margin slipped to 35.4% from 39.4%. Two insiders sold on 11/20 under 10b5-1 plans. Oppenheimer initiated at $30 on 11/19 and the pop faded within days.
gappers.why: Mechanism is competitive displacement plus a withdrawn guide. Pulled guidance removes the forward anchor analysts were paying for, and a credible report that primes could be handed to GM/Ford attacks the core thesis that UMAC owns the US drone component supply chain. Insider selling into weakness and faded analyst initiations confirm nobody is defending the price.
gappers.impact: Mixed. 2.6M shares is the lightest volume in the top 5, so the gap is easier to fade on a headline denial, but the damage is structural rather than one-day: guidance withdrawal is not a headline that expires. Sector read-through is clear and already moving - RCAT -9%, ONDS -4% on the same WSJ story, and ONDS is rank 6 on today's own list.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing today, but per TRADING-STRATEGY.md's sector rule the drone complex is the one group here with two separate failed catalysts in a week (Oppenheimer $30 init faded, Q3 beat sold), which argues for exiting/avoiding the sector rather than entering it. R:R is the weakest of the five: a 7-10% stop at $8.24 sits inside daily noise for a name moving 7-10% a day, so the stop gets taken out before any 2:1 target. Pass.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: SHORT_TERM: the Pentagon/GM story is a headline that could be walked back, and the stock is 47% off its highs well below the 200-SMA - no long thesis survives a withdrawn guide.

gappers.catalyst: Fell ~9% on 11/24 as HPE warned of prolonged component shortages and the Monday AI-power rally unwound; Morgan Stanley called the selloff a buying opportunity (Overweight, $335 PT).
gappers.catalyst_detail: BE rose 18.1% on Monday 11/23 to close $168.15 on the Nvidia CEO reinstatement, then fell ~8-9% on 11/24 and gapped down again to $145.50 pre-market. The driver is HPE's warning of prolonged component shortages - HPE management said supply, not demand, now determines how fast backlog converts to revenue - which Morgan Stanley flagged as a cost risk for data-center power suppliers. Separately, Truist initiated BE at Hold on 11/22. Fundamentals are the strongest of the top 5: 2026 guidance has been raised three times to $4.4-4.6B revenue, Q3 revenue +138% y/y, and Morgan Stanley stayed Overweight with a $335 target.
gappers.why: Mechanism is input-cost and timing risk, not lost demand. Component shortages push out revenue recognition and squeeze margins on a backlog that is already sold, so the market is discounting the pace of the AI-power buildout rather than its existence. The Truist Hold initiation removed a marginal buyer at the same time.
gappers.impact: This is the one name where the move looks more like a one-day-plus overshoot than a thesis break: 13.7M shares is elevated but the catalyst is third-party (HPE) and the company's own guidance is going up, not down. Read-through is the whole AI-power group - FCEL -10%, PLUG -5% on the same tape - so this is a sector de-rating, and it is still the 3rd day of a reversal from a +18% spike, meaning it can keep going.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Best-quality name on the list and the only one with a LONG_TERM read, so it is the one slot worth reserving - it would displace CRWV/NBIS, which are the same AI-infra theme but with credit risk instead of raised guidance. At a $145 price the 20%-of-equity cap (~$20k) permits ~137 shares, and a 10% stop near $131 against the $168 prior close is roughly 1.5:1 - under the 2:1 minimum, so NOT actionable today. It only clears 2:1 if entered nearer a flushed low with a defined swing stop. Watch, do not chase the gap.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: LONG_TERM: the catalyst is structural (AI data-center power demand with thrice-raised guidance) and fits the Early-cycle Technology/Industrials row of the sector-rotation table - worth a multi-day swing IF a later /trade check confirms the Confluence rule and price reclaims the 200-SMA.

gappers.catalyst: Drone complex sold off on the WSJ Pentagon/GM report (ONDS -4% on 11/24) on top of post-Q3 concerns over falling margins, rising losses and equity-raise dilution despite record $167.5M Q3 revenue and an $835M backlog.
Debt-funded AI buildout is the market's stress test: 5y CDS jumped ~7% to ~356bp, >$117B long-term debt against $90-95B planned data-center spend, with the stock now ~53% off its peak.
Fell 8.6% on 11/24 to a 52-week-low area after the Q3 miss (EPS $0.76 vs $0.78, revenue $1.99B vs $2.04B) and flat Q4 guidance of $1.9-2.0B; B. Riley cut its target to $38.

Post-Q3 derating continues: revenue +109% y/y to $290.8M but EPS of $0.02 missed by a cent, and on 11/10 Northland cut to $15, Craig-Hallum to $10 and Needham to $15; securities class-action notices remain an overhang.

Quantum complex extends its slide (IonQ/D-Wave down with it) after Q3 revenue fell 27.5% y/y to $1.41M vs ~$3.5M expected and the CEO conceded none of the sector can yet demonstrate ROI over classical computing.
